answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule: each identity’s action vector across epochs is compared, and identities whose vectors drift beyond a set distance are throttled. An attacker must hold a clone on the same nectar of consistent behaviour, since a sudden shift triggers the threshold. That constraint forces every clone to sit on a narrow ledge of near-identical history, so each fake identity needs its own vault of maintained records and matching activity, multiplying the per-identity cost by the number of epochs tracked.
